facts.statement: The fossil remains of Taubatornis were found in the Tremembé Formation within the Taubaté Basin in São Paulo state, Brazil.
facts.quote: Taubatornis is an extinct genus of teratorn from the Late Oligocene to Early Miocene (Deseadan) Tremembé Formation, in the Taubaté Basin, São Paulo state, Brazil.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Taubatornis is Taubatornis campbelli.
facts.quote: The type species is T. campbelli.

facts.statement: Taubatornis is the oldest known member of the Teratornithidae family, dating to approximately 25 million years ago.
facts.quote: It is the oldest known member of the family, about 25 million years old.

facts.statement: The existence of Taubatornis supports the hypothesis that the Teratornithidae family originated in South America.
facts.quote: The presence of a member of this family with this age supports the hypothesis of a South American origin for the Teratornithidae.

facts.statement: Taubatornis is classified within the bird family Teratornithidae.
The genus Taubatornis was named by Olson and Alvarenga in 2002.
The time range for Taubatornis is estimated between 27.3 and 23.04 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chattian to Chattian (27.3 to 23.04 million years ago)
